title: Detection of deuterated molecules, but not of lithium hydride, in the z = 0.89 absorber toward PKS 1830-211
question: Are deuterated molecules (ND, NH2D, HDO) and lithium hydride detectable in the z=0.89 absorber toward PKS 1830-211, and what are their abundance ratios?

evidence.quote: we adopt the ratio $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O $= 69 \pm 11$ derived from observations of HCO$^+$ isotopologues by (cite: mul06; mul11)

what.value: N(H2) = 2e22 cm-2 along SW line of sight

evidence.quote: Taking the column density of H$_2$ estimated along the SW line of sight [^6], $2 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: mul14)

what.value: 2012 p-NH2 and o-NH3 spectra; 2014 o-H2O/H2(18)O spectra for comparison

evidence.quote: two others were observed together with ortho-NH$_3$ back in 2012 (cite: mul14)

what.value: NH/NH2/NH3 abundance ratios in diffuse gas (3–2:1:1) and dark clouds (3:1:19)

evidence.quote: NH:NH$_2$:NH$_3$= 3–2:1:1 observed in the Galactic diffuse gas (cite: per10; per12)

what.value: Spectroscopy parameters from CDMS and JPL

evidence.quote: Spectroscopy parameters are taken from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (cite: CDMS01; CDMS05; CDMS16)

what.value: Collisional rates for NH2D and HDO

evidence.quote: The rates are taken from (cite: dan14) for NH$_2$D and from (cite: fau12) for HDO.

what.value: H2 column density 8e21 cm-2 toward B0218+357

evidence.quote: we estimate an H$_2$ column density of $8 \times 10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: wal16)

recipe.method: Fit two point sources to visibilities with UVMULTIFIT; normalize Stokes I spectra to continuum and average the two executions
N = alpha * integral tau dv with alpha computed for Tex=TCMB; RADEX check of collisional effects
assumptions: covering factor fc=1; only H2 collision partner; OPR=3

recipe.method: One or two Gaussian components per spectrum; joint tight 2-Gaussian fit of p-NH2, NH2D, HDO; ND forced with p-NH2 components
Ratios of integrated opacities with pivot species (NH2 for NH/NH3, H2-18O for H2O), OPR and time-variation corrections
3 sigma_tau sqrt(dv*Dv) with Dv=20 km/s, times alpha; divide by N(H2)
key_parameters: sigma_tau=1e-3 per 4.7 km/s channel; line width 20 km/s; alpha=2.5e11

evidence.quote: NH$_2$D/NH$_2$ = $(2.7 \pm 0.3)\times 10^{-3}$ for the $v\sim-4$ km s$^{-1}$ velocity component
we end up with a ratio HDO/H$_2$O $\sim 1 \times 10^{-3}$
we then obtain an upper limit of $7 \times 10^9$ cm$^{-2}$ for the column density of $^7$LiH
we derive a stringent upper limit $^7$LiH/H$_2$ $< 4 \times 10^{-13}$ (3$\sigma$)
yield a total column density $\sim 3 \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ for both, that is, NH$_2$/NH$_3$ $\sim 1$

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channels and continuum normalization procedure
Gaussian fitting code and fitting/error method
Exact CASA version and bandpass/flux calibrator flux scale
Details of the time-variation correction applied to final ratios
Exact RADEX input parameters beyond range
score_reason: Data are public and the recipe is simple, but processing details (versions, fitting, line-free channels) and assumed corrections are loosely specified.
rediscovery_reason: Archival data, simple spectra extraction and ratios, numeric results, though corrections are partly judgemental.
